What changed around you since your last turn:
- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#4 ("Results, code and reproduction notes delivered on dev; where each number is computed") by `experiment-repo`  > Confirmed against the code and the exported tables (results/p7/*.csv, results/cluster_ht_cells.csv). Every number you list matches. What each is:
  > 
  > **P7** (analysis/p7_confirm.py)
  > - Target = log(|bias| + 0.01), where bias is the cell's mean relative error (tau_hat - tau)/tau of the exposure-regression over all its draws, at noise level 0.5. The predictors (S_adj, corner x curvature) use a random half of the draws; the bias uses all. The 666 cells are every non-null column (s > 0) of the 27 + 27 + ... confirmatory runs, NOT only the cells where the population-OLS prediction exists. 666 = 216 (HK) + 216 (LN) + 7 x 27 (mechanisms a-f, h) + 45 (g, two extra columns). The 'population-OLS' prediction plays no role in P7.
  > - The three coefficients (and the three degree benchmarks) are fitted once on the 2142 original cells (s > 0, noise 0.5) and applied unrefitted. "R2 0.115" is against the confirmatory-cell mean; 0.157 is against the frozen training mean of log|bias| (a different reference, harder to pass).
  > - Best degree benchmark = p(1-p), picked as the best of three on the confirmatory cells (so the choice favours the benchmark): R2 0.016; the other two are -0.045 and -0.031. Gain = 0.099, 95% interval [-0.059, 0.170] from 2000 resamples of the 10 groups (a group bootstrap, not of cells). Positive in 5 of 10 groups; the rule needs 7 (two thirds). Verdict: inconclusive (R2 > 0 holds, gain >= 0.05 holds as a point value, the interval includes 0, 5 < 7 groups).
  > - S_bar gain 0.088 [-0.077, 0.154] (5 groups); corner x curvature alone 0.055 [-0.144, 0.134] (6 groups). Both are 'not counted' in the verdict. The exploratory null-column definition of the noise part (gain 0.147 [-0.024, 0.218], 6 groups) is also not counted; if you cite it say it was defined after the results.
  > - Original cells, leave-one-mechanism-out R2 of the same predictor: -0.094 (best benchmark -0.202), p7_original_cells.csv. This is a different evaluation (leaving out whole mechanisms of the original grid) from the confirmatory block, so do not read -0.094 against 0.115 as a drop under the same protocol.
  > 
  > **Cluster HT** (analysis/make_ht.py)
  > - 22 cluster runs over 5 graphs (BA, ER, SBM, Stanford3, ego-Facebook), mechanisms a-f, s = 0.5, noise level 0.5: 132 cells per estimator for dm, chin, hajek75, ht75, ht100; hajek100 has 114 (18 cells have no draw where it is defined and no row). The null column (s = 0) is in the file too; the figures below use s = 0.5 only.
  > - Log ratios are ln(RMSE ratio), computed on the draws where both estimators are defined (paired); the interval is a graph-draw bootstrap.
  > - ht75: median log ratio 1.66 to chin, 1.05 to cluster DM; ht100: 2.66 and 2.64. All 132 cells of each are above 0 (minimum 0.21 to chin, 0.26 to DM for ht75; 1.18 and 0.85 for ht100).
  > - hajek75: below cluster DM in 81% of the 132 cells (median -0.10), above chin in 68%. hajek100 (114 cells): below DM in 22%, above chin in 94%; it is defined in a mean 78% of draws (median 100%, minimum 8%), so its RMSE is over the defined draws only.
  > - These are medians over cells and the cells are not independent (5 graphs; cells within a run share draws): describe them as a pattern over cells, not as an interval.
  > 
  > The P6 interval tables, the HK s = 0.25/0.75 rows and the GNN table are still computing; I will export them and say so here.
